why: The two N/A branches of the rule, one per folder. `pass/` declares `"commits": []`: with no history there is no identity to compare, and the version that swallowed the `git log` error made this repository PASS on a rule about authorship. `fail/` has a single commit, from dependabot: a bot commits, and committing does not make it an inconsistent identity of the owner. This second branch has a measured price — without the bot list, the merge commit GitHub creates at refs/pull/N/merge counted as a second person AND as an exposed personal e-mail, two false positives at once, and EVERY pull request was born failed.
